editorial:
Imagine you are a detective who just wants to do her job, but every lead you follow takes you deeper into a system that doesn't want the truth to come out. You follow a tough female cop as she tries to figure out why a bright high school girl named Sohee took her own life. It starts as a simple police case, but it quickly turns into a stressful look at how companies treat their workers. The movie feels very real and heavy, making you feel the frustration of the characters as they hit wall after wall while trying to find justice.

The acting is top-notch and makes the whole story feel authentic. You will love how the mystery unfolds, though be warned that it is more of a slow burn than a fast action flick. It can be a bit sad, but it is an important story about standing up for what is right.
endingExplained: At the end, you find out that the school and the company worked together to hide how much Sohee suffered. They lied about her hours and treated her like a number instead of a person. Even though the detective finds the truth, the system is so strong that it is hard to get a real win. It ends on a sad note, showing that many other students are still trapped in the same cycle.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves realistic mysteries and stories about social justice.
